source.subject: science

source.notes: A bank of practice items (not an examination paper): 'Competency-based education for CBSE, Item Bank: Science Class 7, September 2021', content created by the British Council; the introduction states there are 47 items. Items are not numbered; each is identified by the item identity printed at its top (e.g. Science7VD2), used here as the question number, with the printed sub-question label as the part. Answers are from each item's own mark scheme (Answer and Guidance columns, joined with ' | Guidance: '). Items map to the NCERT books current in 2021; chapters were mapped to the current syllabus (Curiosity, Grade 7) and must be confirmed. Items on soil conservation, wind, irrigation sources, fuses/electromagnets and plant reproduction have no matching current chapter (chapter null). Several items print totals that differ from the sum of their parts (flagged per question). Figures are not reproduced.
source.usage: Official CBSE item bank, freely available on cbseacademic.nic.in for teachers to use as they wish; question text reproduced for study with attribution and a link to the original. Figures are not reproduced.

questions.text: Study the given image carefully and answer the following questions. Determine any two harms caused to soil due to acid rains.

officialAnswer.text: The harms caused by acid rains to soil are 1. Soil becomes highly acidic and releases toxic substances into the soil thereby affecting the plant growth. 2. questions.text: Identify two common natural sources of water for irrigation of crops.

officialAnswer.text: Any two from: Rivers Lakes ground water Wells rains. | Guidance: Any two of the given sources is a correct answer. Manmade water bodies, dams , canals and are not natural sources so are incorrect answers and will not be given marks.

questions.text: State two causes responsible for the depletion of the ground water and explain how they reduce the amount of ground water.

officialAnswer.text: Any two cause-explanation pairs from the following: 1.Deforestation (1) leading to irregular rains which decrease recharging of the ground water. (1) 2. Increased construction (1) which leads to prevention of seeping of surface water or rainwater through the soil to recharge of ground water (1) 3.Increased consumption of ground water for growing agricultural needs (1) due to irregular or scanty rains which leads to over consumption (1) 4.Increase in number of industries (1) due to growing demands leads to over consumption of ground water (1) 5. Growing dependency on ground water for household consumption (1) leads to over consumption of ground water (1) | Guidance: Explanation marks are for saying if the cause reduces recharge or increases consumption. A cause without explanation or vice versa is given one mark.

questions.text: Describe the consequences of acid rains on ground water and on crops.

officialAnswer.text: 1. Increase of acidity in groundwater 2. Increase in toxic chemicals in groundwater 3. Leaching of nutrients from the soil 4. Direct harm to crops (e.g. crops die, quality diminished)
